I thought the score was sometimes great, other times mediocre. It didn't have the soulful aspect of the first movie. It corresponded to the world they showed, sometimes stunningly beautiful but again felt less romantic than the first. They were going for a hopeless dystopian city and got it. But it seemed to achieve this feeling through angry synthesizer noises and harsh city aesthetics; not the same steamy Hong Kong noir of the first movie. They wanted high contrast between the elite and the rest of the city dwellers. This was well accomplished with set design, visuals, costumes, and score. But sometimes the score and sets felt discordant. Consider the harmony between Terrell's office in the first movie, it fit the world. Niander Wallace didn't achieve the same feeling. But with the exception of the city overhead shots and the place with the children, the cinematography was stunning and well considered.

Costumes were great, Luv's and Joi's were perfect. Great attention to detail and nods to the past. K's was good. It struck a balance with functional and his station in life; he did not have a fucking scarf or some other doily shit. There was one CG face scene (if not it it looked like it) but it must have been a tough choice to change the shot and the feeling of the scene or keep it. You may not notice it depending on how much high end vidya you play.

Acting was overall solid to plus-good. Luv and Joi (Sylvia Hoeks and Ana de Armas) were stand outs, top notch. We need more people like them in leads; more acting ability and less getting the role due to who they are. Maybe I'll grow to like gosling more upon further viewings. I did hear the script was written with him in mind, but I'm not sure why. Leto is said to have studied the manners of tech moguls in silicon valley and their ilk for his role. He certainly got close to the uncanny valley (did he watch the zuck?). I think my issues with Wallace are due to the story and not his acting.

Story seemed to leave some parts on the editing room floor, but I'm ok with the narrator only seeing parts of a whole. It didn't feel obtrusive. Some parts maybe stayed in because of the beauty and not story, but maybe for mystique. I think they walked a line with Wallace, maybe they came down on the wrong side of 'for the greater good' and an aloof sadist. Tyrell he is not. There were misplaced/unnecessary sexual undertones with K's boss. It could have been the story or it could have been Robin Wright feeling like Clair Underwood. Additionally, there was only one gratuitous sex scene and it was pretty PG. Slight spoiler

On the whole somewhere between A- and B+, not bad in the current movie situation. Generated emotion, thought, and reflection on the human condition. Art worth the 1/2 price tickets on Tuesdays and likely the full price. I think it will hope up to repeated viewings.
